full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Karim J: This Rule issued on an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the order dated 21-1-95 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous (Arbitration) Case No. 79 of 1994. 

 2. Opposite party No. 1 Zakir Construction & Co. Ltd. was the 1st party in Miscellaneous (Arbitration) Case No. 79 of 1994 filed under section 11 of the Arbitration Act and petitioner Bangladesh Water Development Board figured as 2nd party in the said Misc. case. Petitioner Bangladesh Water Development Board through its Executive Engineer, O & M. Division-II, floated a tender for construction of 8 Vent RCC Pipe Sluice Gate at 13.65 Km of Greater Dhaka City Flood Protection Embankment in connection with flood protection of greater Dhaka City during 1989-91. A work order for Taka 1,75,00,000.00 was issued in favour of opposite party No. 1. Subsequently a dispute about enhancement of rates for payment of bills arose and the parties agreed to settle the dispute through arbitration and accordingly, Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim was appointed the sole arbitrator. The proceedings, however, could not be completed because of adjournments and other reasons. On 24-1-94 opposite party No. 1 Zakir Construction & Co. filed an application under section 11 of the Arbitration Act before the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, for appointment of a new arbitrator in place of Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim and the application was registered as Misc. (Arbitration) Case No. 79 of 1994. Thereafter opposite party No. 1 filed another application for appointment of Mr. Maksudur Rahman as arbitrator citing him as a Justice in place of Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim, The petitioner filed an application opposing the prayer of opposite party No. 1 for change of the arbitrator and appointment of Mr. Maksudur Rahman as the arbitrator. In the meantime Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim expressed his desire to be relieved of his responsibilities as arbitrator and the learned Subordinate Judge under his order dated 26-8-94 relieved Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim of his responsibilities as arbitrator and directed the parties to suggest two names each for appointment as arbitrator. The petitioner suggested names of two engineers and the opposite party suggested two names, namely, Mr. Justice K M Sobhan and Mr. Justice Maksudur Rahman (citing him as a Justice). On 4-8-94 the learned Subordinate Judge appointed Mr. Maksudur Rahman as sole arbitrator holding that Memo No---- dated 15-4-89 of petitioner Water Development Board provides for appointment of a Justice in respect of claims exceeding Taka 50,00,000.00. It is stated in the revisional application that the learned Subordinate Judge did not take notice of a subsequent memorandum of the Water Development Board providing for appointment of a Chief Engineer or an Addl. Chief Engineer as an arbitrator in respect of claims exceeding Taka 50,00,000.00. It is also alleged in the application that Mr. Maksudur Rahman, who was appointed an Additional Judge of the Supreme Court, High Court Division, tendered his resignation before confirmation and since then he has been practicing as an Advocate of the Supreme Court and the Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in appointing Mr. Maksudur Rahman citing him as a retired Judge of the Supreme Court. On 15-9-94 the petitioner filed an application before the learned Subordinate Judge (Annexure-A) asserting that Mr. Moksudur Rahman, having resigned as a Judge before his confirmation and being a practicing lawyer since then, was not a proper person for appointment as an arbitrator and that this appointment of Mr. Maksudur Rahman by the court was erroneous. In that application the petitioner prayed for appointment of an Engineer from the list earlier submitted by them and a retired Judge of the Supreme Court as arbitrators in the case. It is alleged in the revisional application that the learned Subordinate Judge did not pass any order on the application on 15-9-94. Thereafter the petitioner filed another application on 18-9-94 (Annexure-B) reiterating the position taken in the earlier petition against the appointment of Mr. Maksudur Rahman as arbitrator as being erroneous with the prayer for appointment of a retired Judge of the Supreme Court in place of Mr. Maksudur Rahman as the arbitrator. The petitioner also filed another application (Annexure-C) before the arbitrator with a prayer for staying the arbitration proceedings till disposal of their application dated 15-9-94 by the learned Subordinate Judge. It is alleged in the revisional application that since Mr. Maksudur Rahman was not willing to wait till disposal of their application (Annexure-A), their lawyer Mr. Tufailur Rahman and Mr. Joynal Abedin participated in the arbitration proceedings on protest. It is further stated that since Mr. Maksudur Rahman without affording proper opportunities to the petitioner and in a great hurry wanted to conclude the arbitration proceedings, the petitioners were compelled to withdraw from the arbitration proceedings on 24-10-94 in the apprehension that they would not get proper justice from him. The petitioner filed another application dated 25-10-94 before the learned Subordinate Judge to stay the arbitration proceedings till disposal of their applications dated 15-9-94 and 18-9-94. But a copy of the application having not been served on the other side, the matter was heard on 26-10-94 when the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the application holding that the conduct of the arbitrator did not show anything that the party would not get justice from him. Thereafter the learned Subordinate Judge under his order dated 6-11-94 directed the parties to pay equally fees for the arbitrator amounting to Taka 40,000.00. Thereafter petitioner Bangladesh Water Development Board filed a revisional application before the High Court Division under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the orders dated 26-10-94 and 6-11-94 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. A Division Bench of this Court disposed of the revisional application in Civil Order No. 4091 of 1994 under the order dated 11-12-94 without issuing any Rule and directing the Subordinate Judge to dispose of the applications filed by the petitioner on 15-9-94 and 18-9-94 by 8-1-95. Thereafter the Subordinate Judge heard the applications dated 15-9-94 and 18-9-94 and disposed of the same under his order dated 21-1-95. It is the case of the petitioner that by passing the impugned order dated 21-1-95 the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not taking into consideration the objection raised by the petitioner regarding the appointment of Mr. Maksudur Rahman as arbitrator and the reasons set forth in their applications dated 15-9-94 and 18-9-94. 

 3. In the counter affidavit filed on behalf of opposite party No. 1, namely, Zakir Construction & Co., the statements and allegations made in the revisional application have been challenged. It is stated in the counter affidavit that at the instance of petitioner Water Development Board, Mr. Justice Maksumul Hakim was initially appointed the sole arbitrator and, as such, subsequent suggestion for appointment of an Engineer as arbitrator was not reasonable. The statement in the revisional application regarding appointment of an Additional Chief Engineer or Chief Engineer as arbitrator for claims exceeding Taka 50,00,000.00 is denied. It is stated in the counter affidavit that the provision relating to appointment of a retired Judge as an arbitrator for claims exceeding Taka 50,00,000.00 as contained in the memo dated 15-4-89 of Water Development Board and the subsequent amendment thereof is a matter to be followed by Water Development Board and not for the court to follow in appointing an arbitrator under section 12 of the Arbitration Act. The case of opposite party No. 1 is that Mr. Maksudur Rahman after being appointed as Additional Judge of the Supreme Court, High Court Division, was confirmed as a Judge, but he tendered his resignation before taking oath as a permanent Judge of the Court. So, the statement of the petitioner that having not been confirmed as a Judge, Mr. Moksudur Rahman was not a fit person for appointment as arbitrator is denied by opposite party No. 1. The statement in the revisional application that by failing to consider the reasons set forth by the petitioner in his petitions dated 15-9-94 and 18-9-94 for appointment of a new arbitrator in place of Mr. Moksudur Rahman, the learned Subordinate Judge made an error of law or caused miscarriage of justice in passing the impugned order dated 21-1-95 is also denied. The petition dated 15-9-94 (Annexure A) for appointment of a new arbitrator in place of Maksudur Rahman and the petition dated 18-9-94 (Annexure-B) for staying the arbitration proceedings were first disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge under his order dated 26-10-94 and finally under the impugned order dated 21-1-95. It is the case of the opposite party that by passing the impugned order, the learned Subordinate Judge committed no error of law or miscarriage of justice to any party. 

 6. Mr. Fazlul Hoque submits that by appointing Mr. Moksudur Rahman as an arbitrator in the case, the learned Subordinate Judge did not commit any illegality and that Mr. Moksudur Rahman was appointed as Assistant Judge and he was confirmed as a Judge of the Supreme Court, High Court Division, though he resigned without acting as a permanent Judge. There is no law or rule that none but a retired Judge of the Supreme Court could be appointed as arbitrator in a case like this. 

 10. It appears from this Memo that in the matter of appointment of an arbitrator for claims exceeding Taka 50,00,000.00 preference is to be given to a retired Judge of the Supreme Court. There is nothing to show from this Memo that none but a retired judge could be appointed an arbitrator. This Memo dated 15-4-89 and a subsequent amendment thereof providing for appointment of a Chief Engineer or an Additional Chief Engineer as arbitrators were issued after issuance of the work order dated 18.3.89 and consequently Mr. Fazlul Hoque submits that the guidelines contained in this memo for appointment of an arbitrator have no application to the arbitration proceeding of the instant case. We find substance in this contention. We have already mentioned that the Memo of Water Development Board provides for only a preference to be given to a retired judge of the Supreme Court for appointment as an arbitrator and does not contain any provision that no person other than a retired judge could be appointed an arbitrator. 

 12. The scheme of section 12, particularly of sub-section (2) thereof, clothes the court with the authority of appointing an arbitrator in its discretion after the parties fail to nominate a common arbitrator. Here the petitioners as well as the opposite party could not nominate a common arbitrator thereby leaving it to the discretion of the court to appoint an arbitrator, namely, Mr. Maksudur Rahman, a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, as an arbitrator. In such a situation the court can, in an appropriate case, go beyond the arbitration clause in making its choice and is not bound to confine its choice to the criterion mentioned in an agreement between the parties. 

 17. The learned Subordinate Judge under the order dated 21-1-95 disposed of the applications dated 15-9-94 and 18-9-94. These two applications mention the same grievance, that Mr. Maksudur Rahman resigned before confirmation as a Judge of the Supreme Court, High Court Division, and that he has been practicing as an Advocate of the Supreme Court. since then. Both the petitions take the common ground that the appointment of Mr. Maksudur Rahman as the arbitrator was erroneous on this score. We have already discussed this ground taken in all these applications (Annexure-A, Annexure-B and Annexure-C). We have similarly held that the memo of the Water Development Board dated 15-4-89 merely gives preference to a retired Judge of the Supreme Court in the matter of appointment of an arbitrator in claims exceeding Taka 50,00,000.00 and that this memo and the subsequent memo about appointment of a Chief Engineer or an Additional Chief Engineer as arbitrator were issued after issuance of the work order on 18-3-89 and, as such, these two memoranda have hardly any application to the facts of the present case. In the impugned order dated 21-1-95 the learned Subordinate Judge has rightly observed that the question whether Mr. Maksudur Rahman was a confirmed or a retired Judge has hardly anything to do with his selection as an arbitrator and that his conduct as an arbitrator did not show anything to support an apprehension of injustice by the petitioner. 

 19. The last point mentioned by the learned Subordinate Judge in the impugned order dated 21-1-95 is, that an award may be set aside under section 30 of the Arbitration Act on the ground of misconduct by the arbitrator and the remedy is open to an aggrieved party before the court makes the award a Rule of the court. On all these grounds the learned Subordinate Judge under his order dated 21-1-95 rejected the applications of the petitioner dated 15-9-94 and 18-9-94. The contention of Mr. Tufailur Rahman that the impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge did not consider the grounds set forth in the applications dated 15-9-94 and 18-9-94 is not correct. We find that the learned Subordinate Judge by passing the impugned order has not committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
